description: Senior CS student specializing in backend systems, GIS, and data mining (Node.js, Python, React, PostgreSQL). For the MODIS & VIIRS Hot Spots challenge, I’m building an automated WGS 84 geospatial pipeline using spatial clustering to resolve 1 km vs. 375 m sensor mismatches into a live wildfire dashboard. Backend and cloud deployment are moving fast—looking for teammates skilled in GIS, Frontend visualization (Leaflet/React), or video storytelling to ship!
summary: We developed the MODIS & VIIRS Thermal Anomaly Harmonizer, a full-stack geospatial web dashboard that unifies Near-Real-Time (NRT) wildfire telemetry from NASA's coarse 1 km MODIS and fine 375 m VIIRS instruments in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) across Türkiye. Because a single fire often triggers one coarse MODIS detection alongside multiple adjacent VIIRS sub-pixel alerts, raw satellite feeds inflate event counts and obscure true fire intensity. Our platform solves this resolution and schema mismatch by normalizing heterogeneous sensor confidence scores onto a unified 0.0–1.0 reliability scale and applying spatiotemporal Haversine DBSCAN clustering per acquisition date to merge overlapping cross-sensor detections into Fire Radiative Power (FRP)-weighted centroids while preserving VIIRS-only micro-hotspots. Finally, an interactive Burning Activity Calendar aggregates daily harmonized FRP and flags statistical fire spikes exceeding $\mu + 1.5\sigma$, giving responders and Earth scientists an actionable, noise-free picture of active thermal anomalies.
details:
Live Application: https://modis-viirs-harmonizer.onrender.com/

Source Code Repository: https://github.com/Hemdi2004/modis-viirs-harmonizer

WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

The MODIS & VIIRS Thermal Anomaly Harmonizer ingests Near-Real-Time (NRT) active fire observations from NASA FIRMS across Türkiye's WGS 84 bounding box (25.5°E–44.8°E, 35.8°N–42.1°N) and reconciles sensor differences through a four-stage pipeline:

1. Multi-Sensor Ingestion & Resilience: Fetches live 5-day MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS NOAA-20 (375 m) NRT CSV streams via the NASA FIRMS Area API with an automatic local telemetry fallback to guarantee zero downtime during field use.

2. Schema & Confidence Normalization: Converts MODIS numeric confidence percentages (0–100%) and VIIRS categorical flags (low, nominal, high) onto a standardized 0.0–1.0 reliability index paired with Fire Radiative Power (FRP in MW).

3. Spatiotemporal Haversine DBSCAN Clustering: Projects WGS 84 latitude/longitude coordinates onto a spherical Earth radius (6,371.0 km) per acquisition date (eps_rad = eps_km / 6371.0). Overlapping cross-sensor detections are merged into FRP-weighted centroids, while isolated VIIRS sub-pixel hotspots remain intact. An interactive radius slider (0.2 km – 5.0 km) lets analysts inspect deduplication sensitivity in real time.

4. Burning Activity Calendar & Anomaly Spike Detection: Aggregates daily harmonized FRP totals and automatically flags statistical fire surge days exceeding the rolling mean plus 1.5 standard deviations (mean + 1.5 * std).

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Emergency responders, forestry teams, and GIS researchers gain an immediate, mobile-responsive operational view that eliminates duplicate cross-sensor alerts while preserving high-resolution 375 m micro-hotspot sensitivity—particularly valuable in wildfire-prone Mediterranean and forested regions such as Karabük and southern Türkiye.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & STACK

- Backend & Data Science: Python 3, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn (Haversine DBSCAN), Requests.

- Frontend & GIS Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet.js (WGS 84 / EPSG:4326), Chart.js, Esri World Dark Gray Base tiles.

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and Render Cloud.

AI / SUPER INTELLIGENCE TRANSPARENCY

AI assistance (Gemini) was utilized during development to accelerate FastAPI/Leaflet boilerplate scaffolding and debugging, while GIS domain design, WGS 84 spatial parameterization, and deployment architecture were directed and verified by the developer.
